> Can you confirm the time in UTC so I can be certain? If it's 09:00 UTC that would be 02:00 PDT for me which won't work — I suspect the 10:00 AM CET you intended is 09:00 UTC.

Hi all — jumping in from CS/ops side. This is a pretty common Google Calendar gotcha around DST and "floating" events. A couple notes and a quick fix: 

- When creating the event, the organizer should explicitly set the event timezone (e.g., Europe/Paris) instead of leaving it "floating." That ensures Google stores the event with a TZ identifier and prevents attendees' clients from converting it inconsistently.
- If you already have an invite that appears wrong, the organizer can: Edit event -> More options -> Event time zone -> select explicit TZ (Europe/Paris) -> Save & send update.
- If someone forwarded the invite, some calendar clients strip TZ info which can cause the event to appear offset for attendees in other regions.

I've attached a screenshot showing the "floating" label and an example of where to set the zone. If it's easier, Sophie, could you re-send the invite with the timezone explicitly set to Europe/Paris (CET) and include John as an attendee directly rather than forwarding? That should fix it.

Alternative meet windows that avoid overnight for all regions: 
- 16:00 CET / 08:00 PDT / 00:00 SGT (next day) — Wed 25 Mar
- 17:00 CET / 09:00 PDT / 01:00 SGT (next day) — Thu 26 Mar

Attachment: screenshot-calendar-timezone.png

Cheers,
